review: 704.5c-1: poison is dealt by combat damage, so the record kind is combat, not resolution; changed record_kind and added combat to the 704.5c triage line.
704.5h-1: setup started in declare_blockers although the first decision declares attackers; set step to declare_attackers and added combat to the 704.5h triage line.
704.5m-2: expected put Pacifism into B's graveyard, but A owns Pacifism; corrected to A's graveyard.
704.5r-1: decision had players pass before the trigger was put on the stack; reordered, and noted that Forge's MaxCounter static may refuse the counter instead of removing it by state-based action.
704.5s-1: setup step was main1 although the decisions pass through upkeep and draw first, so the lore counter would never be added; set step to draw and fixed the decisions.
704.5t: triage marked it out_of_scope though venture cards and dungeons are playable in a Forge two-player game; reclassified as mechanical/needs_new_fields and added scenario 704.5t-1.
704.5v: the skip reason was wrong, since countering the Siege's defeat trigger isolates the graveyard branch; replaced the skip with scenario 704.5v-1 (Lightning Bolt then Stifle).

704.5y: the skip reason was wrong, since gaining control of a Siege makes its protector illegal in a two-player game; replaced the skip with scenario 704.5y-1 (Confiscate) and set the triage record kind to playability.
704.5x: skip reason reworded to the actual reason (protector assigned on entry, no effect makes a permanent become a battle).

skipped.reason: no non-Siege battle has been printed, so no Forge card can illustrate it
every battle gets a protector as it enters (310.9a) and no Forge card turns a permanent already on the battlefield into a battle, so a battle without a protector cannot arise in a two-player game

scenarios.title: State-based checks repeat until no action applies

setup.notes: Goblin King gives Goblin Piker +1/+1, so Goblin Piker is a 3/2 with 1 damage marked.

decisions: A casts Shock targeting Goblin King, tapping Mountain.
Both players pass; Shock resolves.

variants.label: piker_damaged
variants.expected: Goblin King is dealt 2 damage and dies in the first state-based check. Goblin Piker is then 2/1 with 1 damage and dies in the repeated check. Both are in B's graveyard before any player receives priority.

variants.label: piker_undamaged
variants.delta: Goblin Piker has no damage marked.
variants.expected: Goblin King dies in the first check. Goblin Piker (2/1, no damage) stays on the battlefield; the repeated check finds nothing to do.

operation.unclassifiable: damage marked on a creature is not a fork-settable fact

scenarios.title: A player's loss and a creature's death in one state-based check
decisions: A activates Pestilence for {B}, tapping Swamp.
Both players pass; the ability resolves and deals 1 damage to each creature and each player.

variants.label: lethal
variants.expected: B is at 0 life and loses the game, which ends at once. Llanowar Elves stays on the battlefield with 1 damage marked. A is at 19 life.

variants.label: survives
variants.delta: B is at 2 life.
variants.expected: B is at 1 life and the game goes on. Llanowar Elves, dealt 1 damage, is put into B's graveyard by the state-based check. A is at 19 life.

detector.none: What the check would do beside the game loss happens after the game is over, and no record shows it: the resolution's effect half stops at the damage, and sba_zone_move leaves out every record whose changes end the game for this reason.

departure.forge_behaviour: GameAction.checkStateEffects first calls checkGameOverCondition and returns once the game is over, so a check that finds a player at 0 life ends the game before performing its other state-based actions: the creatures it would destroy stay on the battlefield.
departure.note: Rule 704.3 performs every applicable action at once: B loses and Llanowar Elves is put into the graveyard together. Accepted because the game is over either way and nothing observable follows in a two-player game; the expected outcomes are Forge's.

scenarios.title: A state-based check ignores a transient 0 toughness in the middle of a resolution

setup.notes: Maro's power and toughness equal the number of cards in its controller's hand. Each library holds at least 10 cards.

decisions: A casts Wheel of Fortune, tapping Mountain and two other lands.
Both players pass; Wheel of Fortune resolves.

variants.label: wheel
variants.expected: During resolution A's hand is empty and Maro is momentarily 0/0, but no state-based check runs then. After resolution A holds 7 cards and Maro is a 7/7 that stays on the battlefield.

variants.label: mind_rot
variants.delta: A's hand holds Mind Rot instead of Wheel of Fortune; A casts Mind Rot targeting A, tapping Swamp and two other lands.
variants.expected: Mind Rot makes A discard the two Plains, leaving A's hand empty. Maro is 0/0 at the next check and moves to A's graveyard.

operation.unclassifiable: different spell cast and different hand

detector.none: The rule is the absence of a state-based check during a resolution. A resolution record holds a snapshot from before it and the events of it, never a mid-resolution state, so a characteristic that is momentarily 0 or less and restored by the same resolution leaves no field or event.

detector.near_miss: A player whose life the resolution lowers stays at 1 or more and does not lose.

scenarios.title: A copy of a spell ceases to exist once it leaves the stack

setup.notes: Only the first sentence of 704.5e (a spell copy) is illustrated; copies of cards in other zones need a cast-from-copy effect.

decisions: A casts Lightning Bolt targeting B, tapping Mountain.
A casts Twincast targeting Lightning Bolt, tapping two Islands; the copy also targets B.
Both players pass; the copy resolves, then both players pass; the original resolves.

variants.label: copy
variants.expected: B takes 6 damage in total. A's graveyard holds exactly Twincast and Lightning Bolt; the copy resolved and ceased to exist and never reached a graveyard.

variants.label: real_card
variants.delta: A's hand holds a second Lightning Bolt instead of Twincast; A casts it targeting B, tapping the other Mountain.
variants.expected: B takes 6 damage in total. A's graveyard holds two Lightning Bolt cards, because the second one is a card and not a copy.

detector.none: No record field or event shows a spell copy ceasing to exist; the copy's removal from the stack is not an event.
